Title: Integrity-protected evidence chain
Statement: Evidence objects (decision records, trails, SML, EIT, CAG snapshots, manifests) MUST be covered by an integrity mechanism that provides tamper evidence, append-only semantics, and deterministic verification steps.

Title: Key custody and rotation
Statement: Signing keys MUST be managed by enterprise-grade key management (KMS/HSM). Rotation schedules MUST be documented. Compromise procedures MUST include key revocation, trust discontinuity signaling, and chain re-anchoring guidance.

Title: Verifier independence
Statement: Evidence MUST be verifiable without proprietary vendor systems. A verification guide MUST document required inputs, verification steps, failure modes, and result interpretation.
ATAL References: Verifiable without proprietary systems; Auditor portability

Title: Minimum event fields for evidence objects
Statement: Evidence objects MUST include event_time (wall clock), monotonic_time (node monotonic where available), sequence_number (per producer), and producer identity.

Title: Declared ordering model
Statement: Deployments MUST declare an ordering model (centralized or hybrid). Reconciliation rules MUST be documented and auditable, covering tie-break rules, clock tolerance, and partition behavior.

Title: Replay and duplication detection
Statement: Duplicate record_id or replayed evidence objects MUST be detectable. The system MUST define how replays are flagged and how investigations proceed.

Title: Controlled invocation surface
Statement: Tool, API, memory, and routing endpoints MUST be reachable only through the ATAL enforcement layer. Any direct access path MUST be blocked using network and identity controls, not only application logic.

Title: Change control for enforcement layer
Statement: Changes to gateway policies, tool registries, envelope evaluators, routing rules, and safety kernel configurations MUST be versioned, peer-reviewed, and recorded as governance events.

Title: Threat model declaration
Statement: Deployments MUST declare attacker classes considered (external, insider, compromised host, supply chain), assumptions and out-of-scope boundaries, and mitigations required to sustain non-bypassable claims.

Title: Field-level privacy protection
Statement: Evidence stores MUST support field-level encryption or structured redaction with integrity-preserving references for sensitive data classes.

Title: Auditor access governance
Statement: Evidence access MUST enforce least-privilege roles, time-bounded access sessions where feasible, audited access logs, and controlled export of forensic bundles.

Title: Retention-by-class policy
Statement: Retention MUST be defined as a function of risk class, data classification, and jurisdictional obligations, with documented deletion and archival procedures.

Title: Evidence store incident posture
Statement: Deployments MUST document breach impact, mitigation, and incident response for evidence stores.

Title: Bypass test suite
Statement: A test suite MUST include attempts for direct tool/API invocation bypass, undeclared memory persistence, unauthorized delegation or routing, tool registry tampering, and evidence tampering and replay.

Title: Evidence reconstruction drill
Statement: An audit team MUST reconstruct a selected incident path using only recorded evidence at least twice per year (L2/L3). At least one drill MUST assume vendor tooling is unavailable (L3).

Title: Kill-switch test and dual-control enforcement
Statement: Kill-switch procedures MUST be tested periodically. L3 deployments MUST enforce dual-control for all kill-switch actions and include at least one live-fire exercise in controlled conditions.

Title: Operator-of-Record and Approver-of-Record role definitions
Statement: Deployments MUST define Operator-of-Record (OOR), Approver-of-Record (AOR) for higher-risk actions, Policy Owner, Evidence Custodian, and Safety Kernel Operator (where applicable).

Title: Separation of duties
Statement: OOR and AOR MUST be distinct identities for higher-risk actions. Evidence Custodian MUST be distinct from Policy Owner where feasible. L3 MUST separate Policy Owner, Safety Kernel Operator, and Evidence Custodian.

Title: Dual control for high-impact actions
Statement: L3 deployments MUST enforce dual control for kill-switch actions, high-impact policy changes, and registry or enforcement configuration changes.

Title: Vendor and integration dependency documentation
Statement: Deployments MUST document all vendor and integration dependencies that form part of the ATAL enforcement boundary, including their assurance claims, version pinning, and update governance.
